67302.en: Let ABC be a triangle and A'B'C' be the medial triangle. Let Ab and Ac be the projections of A' on AC and AB respectively, and define Bc, Ba and Ca, Cb cyclically. The Euler lines of ABcCb, BCaAc, CAbBa concur in X_20417. Morevoer, the circumcenters of the triangles ABcCb, BCaAc, CAbBa, together with X_20417, lie on a circle, CSC, having center X_140. (Benjamin Warren, March 2, 2025)
no: The circle CSC is the complement of the Steiner circle, which passes through the vertices of the Steiner deltoid of the medial triangle. The circle CSC also passes through the points X(i) for i = 11623, 16534, 20417, 20418, 67277, 67278. The radius of CSC is 3R/4, where R is the radius of the circumcircle. The point X_37302 is the isogonal conjugate of the perspector of CSC. (Peter Moses, March 2, 2025)

67400.en: Note: 𝒞(P, Q) is a rectangular hyperbola if Q lies on the tripolar linear of the isogonal conjugate-of-the cross difference of-(P and the Orion transform of P).
re: X_67400 = {X(i),X(j)}-harmonic conjugate of X(k) for these (i,j,k): {2, 7779, 44373}, {325, 9182, 2}
no: This preamble and centers X_67401-X_67413 were contributed by César Eliud Lozada, March 10, 2025.

The following theorem is due to **Dao Thanh Oai** (March 6, 2025): Let ABC be a triangle and P, Q two distinct points. Let :g:`A_{p}B_{p}C_{p} << A_p B_p C_p >>` be the cevian triangle of P. Parallel lines to AP, BP, CP through Q cut BC, CA, AB at A'_{q}, B'_{q}, C'_{q}, respectively. Let A"_q, B"_q, C"_q be the reflections of Q in A'_{q}, B'_{q}, C'_{q}, respectively. Then: :g:`A_{p}B_{p}C_{p} << A_p B_p C_p >>` and A"_q B"_q C"_q are perspective, with perspector Z(P, Q)=CevaConjugate(P, Q). Points {A"_q, B"_q, C"_q, P, Q, Z(P,Q)} lie on a conic 𝒞(P, Q).
